doc.title: Bill Allred interviewed by Monk Rowe, Orlando, Florida, February 24, 2017

title: Hiring musicians who read and improvise
summary: He wants players who read and improvise, modeled on Billy Maxted, Matty Matlock and the Bobcats.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Big band discipline versus small-group freedom

blocks.x: Yeah. You led me to a question about being a band leader. And there’s a couple of things I want to ask you. First of all, what requirements, what do you require of a musician in order to hire them to be in your band.

Well I mean the band that I put together, which started pretty much as the Rosie O’Grady’s band, then the guy that owned the place sold it and you could see that it was kind of going, where in 1990 a bunch of us left there and we still had a couple of festivals that we’d been invited to, so we just kept that going and then — so I came up with this band. I really liked what Billy Maxted did, Matty Matlock and then Bob Crosby’s Bobcats that in other words they read music but they also played jazz you know. So I had to get somebody that could read pretty well. Not symphony, standards, but could also improvise. And that’s what we were selling for a long time. And I got hell for it. This is the stupidest thing. But we were playing down in — I don’t want to fill up with a bunch of junk, but we were playing down in South Florida somewhere with a bunch of local guys, no music, it was a jam thing, a good jazz group. And so we got down to the gig and I’m stepping down off the stage and this lady came up and got right in my face and she said, “See how good you can play without your sheet music?” Probably she didn’t like —
She didn’t want to see music stands on the stage.

No. She thought that was stupid you know. And there are people to this day that if you are reading music that’s not jazz. And I mean if that’s all you do, if nobody ever solos, but I mean all the big band arrangement, all it is is a framework for the solos you know. © Fillius Jazz Archive -10-
And that’s what we did. And we did it for 26 years. And it seemed to work for us. But there were those that thought just give me guys that are going to play you know.
